item.title: Packers’ Matt LaFleur applauds ‘savant’ Jonathan Gannon after beating Panthers
item.description: Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images Packers’ Matt LaFleur applauds ‘savant’ Jonathan Gannon after beating Panthers appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Green Bay Packers survived the late rally of the Carolina Panthers to notch a 27-19 victory at Lambeau Field on Thursday. Jordan Love went 30-of-41 for 288 yards and three touchdowns, while Josh Jacobs scored two touchdowns on 21 carries and six receptions. The defense played a huge part in crunch time, including sacking Bryce Young in the last 20 seconds to seal the hard-earned win. Coach Matt LaFleur credited the defense, finding the perfect word for defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon , as reported by Sports Illustrated’s Bill Huber. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “LaFleur uses the word ‘savant’ about Jonathan Gannon,” wrote Huber on X. The defense hummed all game long, sacking Young six times and forcing two turnovers. Gannon is in his first year in Green Bay, energizing the defense with his tactical flexibility and ability to maximize talent. Like LaFleur, Evan Williams gushed about Gannon, stressing that it is a “big trust thing.” “JG feels confident in each of us, which is big. In those big plays, you want a coordinator who is not playing scared. He’s a guy who’s, in the biggest of moments, calling different people’s numbers. He always says players, not plays,” said Williams in the video posted by The Fan 107.5’s Marques Eversoll. “He trusts us to win, and when you feel that type of trust from a coordinator going into a game, it allows you to play free.” Evan Williams continues to rave about Jonathan Gannon. #Packers defense is hummin. pic.twitter.com/ASrmNLQl9B — Marques Eversoll (@MarquesEversoll) October 30, 2026 The Packers have held opponents to below 20 points in their last five games. They improved to 5-3, while the Panthers fell to 3-4. Green Bay will visit the New England Patriots in Week 9. Related: Packers’ Jordan Love sends congrats to Brewers for taking home first World Series title Related: Packers’ Josh Jacobs explains what misinterpreted TD celebrations actually meant

item.title: The 12 strangest science stories we can’t stop thinking about
item.description: The warty comb jelly has an anus that comes and goes Andrey Nekrasov/imageBROKER.com​/Alamy There are some stories that stay with you forever, the big scientific moments that change the course of history. These are not those moments – but we can’t stop thinking about them anyway. Push my button Surgeon Stuart Meloy was performing a pain-relief operation on a woman’s spine when she started exclaiming emphatically. “You’re going to have to teach my husband to do that,” the woman said. This inspired Meloy to invent an implant to help women who are unable to achieve orgasms in the usual way. New Scientist broke the news in 2001, sparking a frenzy of worldwide media excitement. But 13 years later, Meloy was still struggling to raise funds for a full clinical trial, and the “orgasmatron” never reached a climax. Monkey pleasure A long-tailed macaque Shutterstock/fiz_zero We aren’t the only primates capable of coming up with creative ways to pleasure ourselves. In a study of long-tailed macaques ( Macaca fascicularis ) in Bali, Indonesia, Camilla Cenni at the University of Lethbridge in Alberta, Canada, and her colleagues filmed hundreds of examples of male and female monkeys using stone tools as sex toys , rubbing or tapping them on their genitals. According to Cyril Grueter at the University of Western Australia, the Balinese monkeys get plenty of food handouts from humans, and this frees up time for sexual experimentation. But some monkeys in other places have unusual kinks, too: another study reported a wild macaque in Japan rubbing its genitals on the back of a sika deer. Advertisement Head transplants In 2015, surgeon Sergio Canavero announced plans to carry out the first human head transplant, intended to extend the lives of people with muscle and nerve degeneration or widespread cancer. He claimed his technique could overcome technical hurdles, including how to fuse the spinal cord and prevent the body’s immune system from rejecting the head. In the following two years, Canavero published animal experiments supposedly backing up his methods, but other surgeons remained highly sceptical . A human head transplant never did happen, but Canavero has reportedly moved on to an even bolder ambition: transplanting a brain into a non-sentient clone. Rats driving Have you ever wondered if a rat can drive a car? Kelly Lambert at the University of Richmond in Virginia has. She and her colleagues built a tiny car with three copper bars that would steer it left, forward or right. Sure enough, 18 rats learned to drive towards food rewards. They even found it relaxing, as measurements of their stress hormones indicated. Lambert proposed that driving challenges could replace traditional maze tests when using rat models to study neuropsychiatric conditions. The sniff test Humans are more similar to rats than we like to think. item.title: Sharks Locker Room: Smith on How “Fun” Inspired Comeback Win, Bystedt “Impressive” in NHL Debut
item.description: Disaster averted. The San Jose Sharks were down 2-0, headed into the third period, against the last-place Vancouver Canucks. They had also gone five periods without a goal and were staring down a potential three-game losing streak. But three goals in the final frame, a pair by Will Smith , reunited with Macklin Celebrini , and Mason Marchment ’s game-winner gave the Sharks a much-needed 3-2 victory. Yaroslav Askarov continued his strong play, stopping 23-of-25 shots. Post-game, Smith spoke on how “fun” inspired the comeback win, Marchment praised Kiefer Sherwood , Filip Bystedt talked about his NHL debut, and head coach Ryan Warsofsky shared when he decided to reunite WillMack. A deeper game story with micro-stats from Stathletes and game action clips, Sharks Insight, will be published soon. Will Smith View this post on Instagram Smith, on who spoke up in San Jose Sharks locker room to fuel comeback, the players or coaches: I think it was both. Everyone stood up and had words to say, but even the coach just said, we’re gripping our sticks too tight. It had been a couple periods without a goal, but we were getting chances. So, like I said, we should go out there and play loose. Smith, on earning a regulation win: It’s huge. We don’t like going to overtime every game. To get one, it was a huge block by Goody there at the end. Put his body in the line. To get that [5-on-6] going while we’re defending is big. Mason Marchment Marchment, on Kiefer Sherwood, who assisted on his GWG: He’s an unbelievable player. He’s hard to play against. He’s in the other team’s face. Not many guys in this league like playing against him. He’s an awesome guy to play with. We had some great looks there in the third together with [Michael Misa]. He’s a fun guy to play with, that’s for sure. Filip Bystedt "Exactly how you dream it to be." Bystedt said his favorite moment from his NHL debut was the Marchment GWG & the Shark Tank crowd pop. He also saw his parents Stefan & Cecilia, who flew in from Sweden, in the stands before the game — Sheng Peng (@Sheng_Peng) October 30, 2026 Ryan Warsofsky Warsofsky, on how much the San Jose Sharks needed this win, emotionally: Yeah, big time, big time. We’ve been frustrated, from the coaches, the players, everyone included, with where our game’s at. There’s a lot of potential for our group, but we have to play a certain way. Proud of the group to come back in the third to win a hockey game. Warsofsky, on when he decided to reunited Macklin Celebrini with Will Smith: About a minute and a half left in the second period. Obviously, we couldn’t generate anything, and we’ve been trying to work with some things within our lines and try to get some chemistry going, and obviously it wasn’t working. It was just time. Warsofsky, on Bystedt’s NHL debut: Thought he was really good. It did not look like his first NHL game. The pace was good, smart, play without the puck. item.title: India squad for New Zealand ODI series 2026: Full updates and team lists for NZ vs IND ODIs
item.description: India squad for New Zealand ODI series 2026: Full updates and team lists for NZ vs IND ODIs originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: India named their ODI squad for the New Zealand tour. The ODI series begins at Eden Park in Auckland on November 4 and ends in Tauranga on November 15. India picked a split squad, as some players will prepare with the red ball for the Wellington Test on November 19. India pick split ODI squad for New Zealand tour as Test preparations loom India's ODI series in New Zealand begins in Auckland on November 4. Five matches will be played across Auckland, Wellington, Hamilton and Tauranga, with the last on November 15. Two Tests follow straight after. The first starts in Wellington on November 19, and the second finishes in Christchurch on December 1. That short gap between formats is a big reason why this selection is being watched so closely. The ODI squad was announced on Friday. The selectors picked a split squad for the first three ODIs an a separate squad for the 4th and 5th ODIs. The fifth ODI in Tauranga is on November 15, and the first Test begins four days later. TOI earlier reported that, like New Zealand, India too will pick a split squad for the ODI series. A few regular India players may prepare with the red ball for a crucial World Test Championship series. Prasidh Krishna has been ruled out of the ODI squad as he is still recovering from a hamstring injury. Mohammed Siraj has been called up to replace the pacer. Meanwhile, Nitish Kumar Reddy has been inducted into the ODI squad for the first match only. The first is on November 4. The last two are both at Bay Oval, on November 13 and November 15. item.title: How talking about Man Utd's cycle of doom became an industry
item.description: Gary Neville and Michael Carrick were Manchester United and England team-mates [Getty Images] Manchester United. More a high-volume content farm than a football club these days. Michael Carrick's starring role in what has become one of the nation's favourite soap operas has been extended for at least another week, with the 45-year-old set to be in charge for Saturday's visit to Chelsea. Good news - you'd think - for Carrick. But even better news for Amazon's All or Nothing camera crews, who have been given "unprecedented" access to document the behind-the-scenes goings-on at Old Trafford this season. United fans will presumably be relieved when the football resumes on Saturday, if only to break up the constant stream of opinion for 90 minutes. But while the wall-to-wall reporting of one of the world's biggest football clubs is hardly new, the unrelenting coverage from former players is a growing phenomenon. It is easier to name the Manchester United legends who don't have a platform from which they scrutinise the club's every move than those that do - and it begs the question whether the club's demise has been industrialised into a content-creating machine. 'It doesn't really help in any way' Whether supporters feel comments from ex-players are damaging or not differs from fan to fan, but what cannot be denied is how difficult it is to escape their views. Sky Sports pundit Gary Neville provided scathing on-air commentary during United's 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth last Sunday, before conducting a post-match podcast in the Old Trafford gantry in which he accused some of their players of being unprofessional. "There's a couple of them... I live in Manchester and they're not that professional, some of them," Neville stated. "I've got no time for them. There's a few of them that don't go to bed at the right time. Don't eat the right things. Don't think about Manchester United every single minute of every single day." But it's digital and streaming platforms that are re-defining a new age of analysis. Neville launched The Overlap in 2021, and its success across video and podcast platforms has seen the channel become one of the most influential outlets in sports media. On Tuesday, Wayne Rooney appeared on Neville's Manchester United-dedicated YouTube channel 'Stick to United' where he said Carrick's players "need a firework up their a***". Neville has since hosted his own The Overlap show where he said managers sometimes need to be sacked "for their own good", while ex-United captain Roy Keane said Carrick and his backroom staff are "lucky boys" to still be in jobs. Neville acquired a network of YouTube channels from United influencer Mark Goldbridge last summer, which has significantly increased the channel's coverage of the club. Largely known for viral clips of his expletive-laden rants during streamed 'watchalongs' of their matches, Goldbridge's YouTube channels had amassed more than 3.7million subscribers. item.title: Ciao, San Siro! AC Milan and Inter announce record-breaking €650m naming rights deal for new Generali Stadium
item.description: AC Milan v FC Internazionale: Semi Final - Coppa Italia - Getty Images Sport The iconic skyline of Milan is set for a historic transformation as the city's two footballing heavyweights prepare to move into a state-of-the-art new home. In a move that signals a massive shift in the financial landscape of Serie A, AC Milan and Inter have officially secured a record-breaking naming rights partnership with Italian insurance giant Generali for their future shared arena. Record-breaking deal for a new era Milan and Inter have agreed a staggering 20-year naming rights contract with Generali, which ESPN reports is worth €650 million (£545m/$725m). The new 71,500-capacity venue will be officially known as the Generali Stadium, effectively replacing the historic San Siro. The clubs purchased the required land from the city last November for €197m , paving the way for the eventual demolition of their legendary current home. Construction is targeted to begin in 2028, with the first matches scheduled for the 2031-32 campaign, pending necessary approvals. Spearheaded by respective ownership groups RedBird Capital Partners and Oaktree, the stadium project also anchors a wider urban regeneration plan featuring new retail, leisure, and green spaces. The massive financial commitment eclipses the $700m agreement struck by Crypto.com in 2021 for the Los Angeles arena shared by the Lakers and Kings. It stands as a monumental boost for the two Serie A giants as they look to modernise and bridge the matchday revenue gap with Europe's elite. A new symbol for Milano. A new home for future generations of fans. Generali Stadium 🏟️ @GENERALI pic.twitter.com/c7D0827E7T — AC Milan (@acmilan) October 29, 2026 Ispirato all'eredità architettonica di Milano e progettato per il futuro. Un nuovo stadio che unisce design, innovazione e sostenibilità in una delle opere più ambiziose mai immaginate per la città. pic.twitter.com/YiQLWaShqO — Inter ⭐⭐ (@Inter) October 29, 2026 Inspired by Milanese heritage In a joint news release, the clubs proudly described the Generali partnership as "one of the largest stadium naming rights agreements in global sport." The statement accompanied the unveiling of the stadium's official renderings, which showcase a striking architectural vision for the city. The design, a collaboration between Foster+Partners and MANICA, draws direct inspiration from "the intricate craftsmanship of the Duomo di Milano." Lord Norman Foster and David Manica, who previously teamed up to design London's Wembley Stadium, have conceptualised a continuous 360-degree bowl split across two tiers. Special attention has been given to the fan experience. The iconic 'Curvas' will feature single, steep walls with seating inclinations of up to 37 degrees to maximise atmosphere and visual impact. According to the release, this aggressive structural approach is designed to "bring supporters closer than ever before to the moments that matter most." Upgrading Italian football's infrastruct

item.title: Hyrox athlete who soiled herself in race tells BBC she put others at risk but says backlash was traumatic
item.description: Watch: 'I made the wrong decision,' Hyrox athlete Joanna Wietrzyk tells BBC An Australian athlete has admitted putting others at risk by continuing to race after soiling herself during an endurance sports event. Speaking exclusively to the BBC ahead of her return to the sport, Joanna Wietrzyk suggested her determination to win the Hyrox race in Beijing in September had clouded her judgement: "It was my decision to continue racing so I take full responsibility for that." Challenged over why she carried on, she said: "I didn't really think about those around me… the decision that I made in hindsight was the wrong decision and I'm truly sorry for everyone that I did affect." The 24-year-old said that the experience and subsequent backlash was "traumatic". She also said she had considered walking away from the sport, in which she holds a world record. Hyrox sees participants alternate between running a kilometre and doing fitness exercises, including a sled push, burpee jumps, indoor rowing, and lunges while carrying a sandbag. The competition has exploded in popularity since it was founded in 2017 in Hamburg, in northern Germany, and is now held across the world. Wietrzyk said she had suffered a bacterial infection from food poisoning [Getty Images] Roughly halfway through her event last month, Wietrzyk suffered a bout of diarrhoea. Images of faecal matter on parts of her body were then shared widely online. Asked whether officials should have stopped her, she said no-one encouraged her to do so at the time. Hyrox's co-founder, Moritz Fürste, has issued an apology saying it had been a mistake not to react immediately during the race. New rules have now been introduced giving race directors the power to remove athletes if their vomit, urine or faeces pose a risk of contamination or threaten the welfare of themselves or others in a race that is primarily held indoors using shared equipment. Although initially defiant in a now-deleted Instagram post, Wietrzyk apologised in the week after the Beijing event and said she would forfeit the win and retroactively withdraw from the race. Due to compete in Hamburg on Friday, she said she was "nervous" about her return and hoped that the high-profile incident would not define her. "I don't want it to become my identity," she said. Joanna Wietrzyk suggested her determination to win clouded her judgement [BBC] In her first interview since Beijing, Wietrzyk said she had suffered a bacterial infection from food poisoning but had gone into the race "feeling fresh, feeling really, really good". "It was a very sudden experience," she told the BBC. "It wasn't until about halfway through the race where everything did transpire... In that moment, right then and there, as a very competitive person… and an elite athlete that I am, my only focus is on racing. "Obviously I did put other people at risk," she admitted. item.title: Azmatullah Omarzai scripts history after walking in at 5/4, smashes T20I world record
item.description: Azmatullah Omarzai produced a stunning rescue act with the bat, smashing a record-breaking century to help Afghanistan recover from a disastrous start and post 221/7 against Zimbabwe in the second T20I at the Sharjah Cricket Stadium on Thursday. Walking in with Afghanistan reeling at 5/4, Omarzai launched a counter-attack that completely changed the course of the innings. He hammered 116 off just 50 balls, striking five fours and 12 sixes at an astonishing strike rate of 232. With the effort, Omarzai registered the highest individual score by a batter coming in at No. 6 or lower in T20Is involving Full Member nations. He went past the previous record of 89, scored by former Afghanistan captain Mohammad Nabi against Ireland in 2017. The record-breaking knock also put Omarzai ahead of Sam Billings (87 against West Indies in 2019), Cameron White (85 not out against Sri Lanka in 2010) and David Miller (85 not out against Pakistan in 2021) on the list. Afghanistan's innings had been in complete disarray after Zimbabwe's bowlers reduced them to 5/4. Several top-order batters departed cheaply, while Sediqullah Atal managed just 17 off 21 deliveries before falling in the ninth over. Omarzai found an ideal partner in Ijaz Ahmad Ahmadzai, and the duo launched a remarkable recovery. They added 142 runs off only 59 balls for the sixth wicket, with Ijaz contributing a blistering 52 off 27 deliveries, including five fours and three sixes. The partnership was finally broken when Ijaz fell with the score at 180. Omarzai continued his assault before being dismissed in the 19th over, having already produced one of the finest rescue acts in Afghanistan's T20I history. Captain Rashid Khan provided a spectacular finish, smashing an unbeaten 25 off just six balls, including four sixes. Mujeeb Ur Rahman remained not out on two as Afghanistan closed their innings at 221/7, scoring at 11.05 runs per over. Rashid also achieved a major milestone during the match, becoming the first bowler to claim 200 wickets in T20Is. Zimbabwe fall short despite Sikandar Raza's century Zimbabwe were unable to overcome the imposing target despite a determined effort from captain Sikandar Raza, who scored his second T20I century. Raza fought till the end, but the visitors ultimately fell short, with Afghanistan's early batting collapse proving to be a distant memory after Omarzai's extraordinary intervention. Tafadzwa Tsiga offered valuable support on his debut, while the dismissal of Ryan Burl dealt another blow to Zimbabwe's hopes. The victory also extended Afghanistan's remarkable dominance in the rivalry, marking their eighth consecutive T20I series win against Zimbabwe. The visitors are yet to win a T20I series against Afghanistan.

item.title: “He Is Made of Glass,” “Eagles Fleeced Patriots”: NFL Fans React As “Washed” A.J. Brown Gets Added to Injury Report With New Concerning Issue
item.description: Jun 2, 2026; Foxborough, MA, USA; New England Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown (1) speaks at a press conference after practice at the team's OTA at Gillette Stadium. © Eric Canha-Imagn Images There were high expectations for A.J. Brown with the New England Patriots this season. The Philadelphia Eagles traded him back in June for a 2027 fifth-rounder and a 2028 first-rounder. However, the wide receiver’s debut in New England has been underwhelming. So far, Brown has missed four games this season due to an injury. He was activated on Oct. 17 and has played in the last two games. However, another concerning update has emerged. On Wednesday, after being listed on the injury report with a knee ailment, the Super Bowl LIX champion missed Thursday’s practice session with the Patriots. Fans on social media shared their reactions to A.J. Brown’s latest injury concern. “The Eagles fleeced them,” a fan said. “Dude is made of glass.. Won’t be drafting again,” another fan wrote. “We tried to tell you he was washed,” one fan commented . Here are some more reactions: In the team’s season-opening loss to the Seattle Seahawks, A.J. Brown suffered a high ankle sprain. He missed the next four games while rehabilitating. In three appearances, the three-time Pro Bowl wide receiver has caught nine passes for 101 yards and no touchdowns. Patriots WR coach Todd Downing shares his thoughts on A.J. Brown On Thursday, New England Patriots WR coach Todd Downing spoke with the media. While discussing A.J. Brown and his performance so far, Downing said that he has faith in the wide receiver despite his underwhelming showcase. “It’s been a small sample size for A.J.,” Downing said. “I think there’s been a lot made about a couple of weeks. My hope, and his hope, and everybody hopes that he gets a little bit of traction. “I’m not worried about where A.J. is at all. Certainly haven’t had the results that we had hoped for, but that doesn’t mean that they aren’t right around the corner.” The Patriots will face the Miami Dolphins on Sunday at 4:25 PM ET. Last week’s 30-24 loss to the Chicago Bears ended their three-game winning streak. item.title: “Exact Opposite of the Ed Reed and Ray Lewis Mentality”: Ravens Fans Slam Kyle Hamilton’s Latest Comments To Address Defensive Struggles
item.description: Kyle Hamilton Ravens © IMAGN Baltimore Ravens safety Kyle Hamilton is receiving flak for his recent comments. During Thursday’s press conference, he was asked to share his thoughts on the team’s defensive struggles this season. Hamilton said that he urges his defensive backs not to push themselves to their limit. He also highlighted the importance of having fun on the gridiron. “I try to relay this message to the DBs, like, it’s a game at the end of the day,” Hamilton said. “I feel like sometimes we’re thinking the whole world’s going to end if something bad happens. That’s not the approach that you need to have in the sport.” “None of our tombstones are going to say, ‘Kyle Hamilton football player.’ It’s a game that we play. We need to have fun doing it. We need to be out there playing the game like we’re playing a game.” Fans questioned Kyle Hamilton’s discipline and dedication to the franchise and football after his comments. Some also compared his mentality to franchise legends Ray Lewis and Ed Reed, considered among the best defensive players of all time. “This is the exact opposite of the Ed Reed and Ray Lewis mentality. … That’s not good,” one fan said. The Ravens drafted Kyle Hamilton with the No. 14 pick in 2022. In August 2025, he agreed to a four-year, $100.4 million extension with $82 million guaranteed. This made him the league’s highest-paid safety until Derwin James signed a three-year, $75.6 million extension with the Chargers. Last season, the two-time All-Pro recorded 105 tackles, one sack, and seven tackles for loss. The Ravens finished 8-9 and failed to make the playoffs. Ravens provide an update on Kyle Hamilton’s injury On Wednesday, Kyle Hamilton missed practice with a knee injury. He was also limited during Thursday’s session, raising questions about his availability for the team’s upcoming game against the Buffalo Bills and Josh Allen. item.title: Kings' overtime coaching overhaul leads to dramatic win over Senators
item.description: Los Angeles Kings players celebrate a goal during a game against the Ottawa Senators on October 29, 2026, at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles, California. The Los Angeles Kings found a way to win a game they shouldn’t have needed to find a way to win on Thursday night. They might have a change in coaching strategy to thank for that. After blowing a 5-1 third-period lead, the Kings defeated the Ottawa Senators 6-5 in overtime behind Quinton Byfield’s game-winner. But almost as interesting as the wild swings of the game was something Drew Doughty revealed after it ended. “It’s the first year in my whole career that we’ve ever actually worked on three-on-three,” the Kings’ captain said. “A lot of credit to the coaches in that area. We worked on it in camp. We worked on it before the season started, and they had a bit of a game plan, which we didn’t really have before either. So a lot of credit to them for making us work on it.” If the Kings ever had an offseason where they needed to improve that aspect of their game, it was this past one. They lost an NHL-record 20 overtime and shootout games in 2025-26, a huge part of the reason they finished with the Western Conference’s second wild-card spot and were swept out of the playoffs in the first round. First-year head coach Peter Laviolette came in and wanted to make sure the Kings didn’t post those numbers again. “There’s definitely a method to the madness, and there’s got to be a buy-in to that, and I think the players bought in,” Laviolette said. “There’s a lot of review that went through it, and there’s things that we talk about prior to games and then after games — the overtime games — and reviewing that. And I think the players have done a really good job of executing them.” Byfield, who scored with a burst of energy straight off the bench, went into more detail about what specifically the Kings focused on in their three-on-three practices. “Just trying to handle the puck as much as we can,” he said. “Obviously taking the right shots. [We] kind of went over it during training camp, some practices as well. You want to possess the puck, kind of tire them out, and let the next guy up come off [the bench]. So they did a great job with that, and I just got lucky there.” “[Last year] we were just taking some shots and missing the net, creating the other way. So we can just maintain it, take the right shots and possess a little more and have it for good opportunities.” The Kings are now 2-2 in overtime this season, an early improvement on last year’s 13-20 mark, and have generally played better in those extra periods. “I actually think that we should be better than 2-2 in overtime, just based on the fact that we controlled a lot — if we played 12 minutes, we thought we controlled 10 of it, but we’re 2-2,” Laviolette said. “So we go back and we look at

item.title: Arsenal set to open contract talks with 'happy' David Raya as Barcelona and Real Madrid stances revealed after goalkeeper's La Liga admission
item.description: Arsenal FC v Everton - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Arsenal are preparing to launch negotiations over an extended deal for first-choice goalkeeper David Raya despite the Spaniard recently admitting he would like to play in his homeland one day. Meanwhile, neither Barcelona nor Real Madrid are expected to make an imminent move for the 31-year-old shot-stopper in upcoming transfer windows. Gunners plan fresh contract talks According to Football Insider , the north London hierarchy want to tie their Spanish custodian down beyond his current 2028 expiration date to fend off any future interest from La Liga. Speculation linking him with Spain's two biggest clubs emerged after he told Spanish media last week that he hopes to play in his native top flight eventually . However, the goalkeeper insisted in the same interview that he remains content at the Emirates Stadium. Spanish giants lack goalkeeping vacancy Having silenced initial sceptics following his move from Brentford to establish himself as the Premier League's standout goalkeeper in recent seasons, Raya registered his fifth clean sheet in eight top-flight outings against Everton last weekend before narrowly losing out on Monday's Yashin Trophy to international team-mate Unai Simon . Explaining why a switch to Spain is unlikely soon on the Transfer Insider podcast, journalist Pete O'Rourke said: "If he were to leave Arsenal, there's no immediate opening for one of the big boys in Spain right now as well. Barcelona have got Joan Garcia, and it looks like Courtois is going to sign a new contract at Real Madrid as well, so I don't see any opening for David Raya right now. "The player is happy at Arsenal, and obviously Arsenal are very happy with him, so I think any potential move back to his native Spain will be probably on the back burner for a while just yet." Arteta jokes about Spanish return Arsenal head coach Mikel Arteta has extracted the best form of Raya's career in north London and has no intention of letting his compatriot depart in the near future . Asked last weekend about his number one's desire to play in their homeland one day, Arteta delivered a lighthearted response: "I think David has to play in Spain at some point...on the beach with his friends in the summer. For the next few years, he needs to play here for Arsenal." Contract extension tops club agenda With both Spanish heavyweights settled between the posts and Arteta determined to retain his star shot-stopper, formal discussions over a renewal past 2028 are expected to get underway shortly. Securing Raya's long-term future will allow the goalkeeper to focus fully on maintaining his impressive defensive record across the autumn schedule. Any potential dream move to La Liga will therefore remain on hold for the foreseeable future.

item.title: DeMarcus Cousins suggests a 'straight-up trade' for Timberwolves after Anthony Edwards' injury
item.description: Photo by David Berding/Getty Images Anthony Edwards is expected to be out for around two months, and that is a huge blow for the Minnesota Timberwolves. The Ant-Man had a phenomenal start to the new NBA season, and he formed an instant connection with LaMelo Ball. The duo looked incredible together. However, Edwards has undergone surgery and will be on the sidelines for a while. The Timberwolves need a solution in his absence, and DeMarcus Cousins has shared an interesting suggestion. DeMarcus Cousins suggests Rudy Gobert for Anthony Davis trade Anthony Davis only joined the Washington Wizards in February this year and made his regular-season debut in the opening game of this season. The former Mavs star has missed several games due to injury in recent years, but on his day, he is up there with the best forwards in the NBA. That is perhaps why Cousins feels the Timberwolves and Wizards should explore a ‘straight-up trade’ that would see Davis and Rudy Gobert switch sides. The former NBA star thinks this move would benefit both parties, as Minnesota would get a replacement for Edwards while the Wizards will have a defensive anchor that they need. Cousins said on Gil’s Arena : “If the Wizards are feeling like it’s not a good move, with everything that’s going on in Minnesota right now with Ant and how much time he’s gonna miss, I say they do a straight-up trade for Rudy and AD. “Man, Rudy’s looking crazy. He’s shooting like 23 per cent at the rim or something like that. If they don’t want to extend AD, they might as well (get him). “I think it would be better for Minnesota all-around. They kind of get the other go-to guy, while Anthony is out, to go along with LaMelo. I think it works for both teams. The Wizards get their defensive anchor. I just thought about it.” Edwards’ absence certainly weakens the Timberwolves, and someone like Davis could guarantee them 20 points a night if they can get him and keep him fit. However, whether the Wizards will accept Gobert after his underwhelming recent performances is anyone’s guess. item.title: Kevin Durant Reacts to Jalen Williams & Cason Wallace Injuries
item.description: Kevin Durant Jalen Williams Cason Wallace Getty Houston Rockets star Kevin Durant reacted to the injuries suffered by Oklahoma City Thunder teammates Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace. Both Williams and Wallace were injured last weekend in a game between the Thunder and the Los Angeles Clippers. Williams has a fractured fibula and a dislocated ankle, and after undergoing successful surgery, will likely be out for the season. Wallace, meanwhile, is also likely out for the season with a torn labrum, a crushing blow to a Thunder team that is looking to win the NBA Championship for the second time in three years. Kevin Durant Reacts to Thunder Injuries Speaking to reporters, the former Thunder superstar Durant shared his sympathies for his former franchise seeing two of its most important players go down with devastating injuries. “I just feel for him. Honestly, this is a brotherhood. We compete at the highest level against each other and we keep that on the floor. But to see one of your brothers in this thing go down with such a gruesome injury, especially at this age and having an injury history last year, just thinking about him. Thinking about his teammates. That’s tough to see, man,” Durant said. “This is a brotherhood. We want everybody healthy. We want everybody on the court doing what they do. But he knows that he has so much support around him. He has so much support around the league. Can’t wait to see him get back. Cason Wallace, too. Get well to all those boys.” Kevin Durant Having Another Big Year for Houston Speaking of Durant, the long-time Thunder star is in his second year with the Rockets, and he’s having another fantastic season for Houston. Through the first five games of the 2026-27 NBA season, the Rockets are 5-0, and Durant has played well, averaging 22.4 points, 6.2 rebounds, and 3.6 assists per game for a Houston squad that looks like it might be a contender in the stacked Western Conference. The Thunder are still one of the best teams in the West, but with Williams and Wallace out, perhaps Oklahoma City’s losses could be Houston’s gain this season. item.title: Sub-plots intensify Blades and Wrexham's rivalry
item.description: Last season's fixtures between Sheffield United and Wrexham were the first league meetings between the sides since the 1982-83 campaign [Getty Images] Just two points separate Sheffield United and Wrexham as the pair lock horns in the Championship at Bramall Lane on Friday night (20:00 GMT). The match-up pits Chris Wilder against his former Southampton youth team-mate Phil Parkinson. And despite the new nature of the somewhat unconventional rivalry between the clubs, the various sub-plots once again make for an intriguing encounter. "It's a tasty game," said Wilder. "It's not historical over 15, 20 to 25 years, it's a recent one, but it's gathered pace along the way." Having not met in 19 years, the Blades narrowly overcame then National League side Wrexham in a fourth round FA Cup replay in 2023, just months before the Red Dragons gained the first of three successive promotions under Parkinson. The Welsh side held their Championship counterparts to a 3-3 draw before losing 3-1 in the replay. But it served as an early signal that Wrexham were determined to compete with the big guns in the near future. "We were talking at a function last night, someone asked me what game typified the Wrexham team and one of them was the home game [against Sheffield United] in the FA Cup," Parkinson said this week. "We lost two players through injury in the first 10 minutes, we were 1-0 down but the determination of the group in that game was incredible. "There was a big gulf between the two clubs at the time, they were top end Championship, one of the best teams. "I think if you can encapsulate everything you'd want in a performance, obviously we didn't get the win, but in terms of the spirit, belief and the hunger, that was all on display." Wrexham urged to board Championship rollercoaster Wrexham fined for fielding ineligible players Wrexham won both meetings between the sides last season, coming from 3-1 down to win 5-3 at the Racecourse Ground in December before again producing a comeback to beat the Blades 2-1 in South Yorkshire in March. "I watched both games back this week," said Parkinson. "The 5-3 was probably one of the best games in the Championship in the whole season for any team. It was a great game of football." Given the significant changes made to both squads during the summer, Wilder is not dwelling on his side's pair of losses to the north Wales outfit last term. "We're not taking too much regarding what happened last year," he said. "We know they've got some really good players. They've got a good management structure that I know well, and they've invested in the summer to make their group stronger." Latest Wrexham news, analysis and fan views Unlucky seven? item.description: Zac Taylor and the Bengals got an encouraging update on Andrei Iosivas. Getty Zac Taylor and the Cincinnati Bengals got an encouraging update on Andrei Iosivas. “Per source, receiver Andrei Iosivas is making good progress on rehab field, with expectation he can return from his left thumb surgery in time for the Steelers game Nov. 15,” CLNS’s Mike Petraglia reported on X on October 30. “Outside chance to return in Spain against Falcons.” That means Iosivas will be out one to two more weeks before being added back to the active roster from injured reserve. The Bengals enter Week 8 at 4-2 on the season. Per source, receiver Andrei Iosivas is making good progress on rehab field, with expectation he can return from his left thumb surgery in time for the Steelers game Nov. 15. Outside chance to return in Spain against Falcons. — Mike Petraglia (@Trags) October 30, 2026 Iosivas has not played since Week 2 against the Houston Texans , a game in which he had one reception for 7 yards. “It’s going to come down to how much pain I can tolerate, and I can tolerate a lot,” Iosivas said, per Bengals.com’s Geoff Hobson on October 29. “I just don’t want to think about it while I’m attacking the ball. It’s getting better.” On the season, Iosivas has a 3-19-0 line for the Bengals Bengals Get Good News on Andrei Iosivas Before Titans Game The 6-foot-3, 210-pound Iosivas also contributes on special teams for the Bengals, albeit sparingly since his rookie season. The Bengals drafted Iosivas in the sixth round with the 206th overall pick of the 2023 draft. He has since become a complement to stars Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. Notably, Chase practiced in full on Thursday after not participating on Wednesday. Bengals Thursday injury report: Ja'Marr Chase back to full. With the Steelers and Cleveland Browns–whom the Bengals will face in Weeks 13 and 18–both at 5-2, Sunday’s tilt is one of several that are close to must-wins. item.title: Farm PC 'maintained' by a 14-year-old dumped support chap in a steaming pile of tech mess
item.description: Welcome to another instalment of On Call, the reader-contributed column The Register publishes each Friday as a cathartic service for readers who know that dealing with tech support BS can be a cow of a job. This week, meet a reader we'll Regomize as "Jason" who told us he had helped an agricultural equipment dealer with his computer issues for about 20 years. "One day this guy called me to ask if I could help at a farm in Yorkshire, where he'd arranged the supply and installation of a fairly substantial system that used a computer to do effectively everything for a few hundred cattle," he told On Call. "That meant individually feeding them, measuring milk yields, planning pregnancies, and periodically submitting all the data to the government." Jason said other tech support folk had tried, and failed, to fix the system. "This had somewhat soured the relationship between the agricultural equipment dealer and the farmer," he punned in his email to On Call. Well punned, Jason. But we digress. "Despite not being fond of wading around in cow shit at four in the morning, I agreed to take a look at the system," Jason told us. By this time he had learned that the farm produced many tons of milk each week, so assumed he would find serious industrial-scale tech once he reached the farm. That assumption was wrong. "When I arrived, the first thing that I found to worry about was that the whole thing was controlled by proprietary software on a single PC running Windows XP – just after Microsoft ended mainstream support." The other things to worry about were all acts of omission: the farm had no backups, no spare PC, and nobody on site to maintain the PC. Jason asked if anyone was responsible for keeping the computer up to date with the security patches and was told the farmer's 14-year-old grandson had done some computer studies at school, so he got the job. That lad had either not discovered, or deleted, the many rather racy videos Jason found on the PC. "When the farmer's wife learned of this, there was what can best be described as a hullabaloo," Jason told On Call. As he dug into the mess, Jason found that the computer was sending milk production data to Her Majesty's Government. He also found that neither the government, nor the farm management software vendor, had bothered to require installation of a firewall. Jason says he installed one, made a few other tweaks, and got the system working. "Everyone seemed pleased, or at least they did until they got my bill," he wrote. "And to be fair, they did pay it promptly." Jason never heard from the farm again. "I don't know if that's because it's still working OK, or if they're just too embarrassed to see me again, or they found someone cheaper who could cope with my recommendations," he wrote. What's the strangest or dirtiest place you've been asked to deliver tech support? Don't cheese us off by holding back! Click here to send us your story so we can milk it for all it's worth in a future instalment of On

item.title: Braves predicted to sign $85M ex-Cubs Gold Glove finalist with power bat after career-best season
item.description: Braves predicted to sign $85M ex-Cubs Gold Glove finalist with power bat after career-best season originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Atlanta Braves won the NL East last season and nearly reached 100 wins, which was a great accomplishment. However, the beginning of the season was plagued by injuries and a suspension. The Braves signed Jurickson Profar two offseasons ago, but the move has been nothing but detrimental. In fact, he has missed 243 games due to suspensions, including a year-long suspension in 2026. “Atlanta Braves designated hitter Jurickson Profar is facing a 162-game suspension after testing positive for a performance-enhancing drug for the second time in the last year, sources told ESPN on Tuesday. Profar, 33, is the sixth player to receive a 162-game ban for PED use since Major League Baseball increased the penalty for two-time offenders to a full season in 2014. He will forfeit the entirety of his $15 million salary," ESPN's Jeff Passan wrote. Heading into the offseason, one of the biggest questions for Atlanta will be how it addresses left field. “The Atlanta Braves enter the offseason with some question marks in their lineup. Last season ended with the bats drying up in October. An answer on Jurickson Profar looms. While Ronald Acuña Jr. and Michael Harris II are everyday outfielders, left field was a rotating spot. It was matchup-dependent, and the needs at shortstop played a role as well in who the options were,” Harrison Smajovits wrote. Finding a left fielder will need to be a priority for the Braves. Sports Talk ATL's Chase Irle believes Atlanta should sign Seiya Suzuki. “He’s done nothing but mash since coming over from Japan, posting an .823 OPS across five seasons with the Chicago Cubs — and like Arozarena, he’s coming off a career-best campaign,” Irle wrote. This would be a significant move for the Braves, as Suzuki is coming off the best season of his career. Not only was his power bat on full display, but he is also a finalist for the Gold Glove Award. Suzuki has just wrapped up his $85 million contract with the Chicago Cubs. Atlanta needs a player like Suzuki in its lineup, and pairing him with Ronald Acuña Jr. could give the Braves two outfielders with some of the strongest arms in baseball. item.title: Florida vs. Georgia game location 2026: Why Cocktail Party is being played in Atlanta
item.description: Florida vs. Georgia game location 2026: Why Cocktail Party is being played in Atlanta originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . One of college football's most heated rivalries between the Florida Gators and Georgia Bulldogs will be played for a 104th time. But this year the annual SEC showdown will be played in a different location than usual. The game, which had been unofficially known as the "World's Largest Outdoor Cocktail Party" since the 1950s, is usually held in Jacksonville, Fla. But for 2026, the game will be held in Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, Ga. In 2027, the game will be held in Tampa, Fla. Here's a look at why the location of the game moved, and when it could return to its usual host city. MORE: Picks against the spread for Week 9's Halloween college football schedule Where is the 2026 Florida-Georgia game? This year's Florida-Georgia game will be played at the Mercedes-Benz Stadium located in downtown Atlanta, Ga. The game was moved from its usual venue, Everbank Stadium in Jacksonville, Fla., as a result of the stadium's renovations that are ongoing. The renovations are set to be completed in Aug. 2028. The game being moved to Atlanta was announced in 2024, as well as the 2027 date set for Raymond James Stadium in Tampa, home of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Although there were some who thought the two games might be played on each team's home campuses, there is a lot more money to be made with neutral-site locations. The game will be played in its usual location, Jacksonville, starting in 2028. According to The Athletic , both Florida and Georgia schools are getting a whopping $7.5 million each from Arthur M. Blank Sports and Entertainment to play the game in Atlanta. Arthur Blank is the owner of the Atlanta Falcons, who also play out of Mercedes-Benz, as well as the Atlanta United of Major League Soccer and the future NWSL team, Atlanta City FC. Both schools will additionally get $1.5 million each from the city of Jacksonville as part of the deal to keep the game there. The current agreement will keep the game at Everbank Field from 2028-2031, with a new deal expected to be reached before 2032 to keep the game there. MORE: College Football Playoff bracket for Week 9: Projecting top four seeds, first-round matchups, bubble teams Florida vs. Georgia stadium details Stadium: Mercedes-Benz Stadium Capacity: 71,000 The stadium in downtown Atlanta is no stranger to hosting big college football events. It is home to the SEC Championship Game each year, as well as the Chick-fil-A Peach Bowl, which hosted the College Football Playoff Semifinal between Oregon and Indiana last season. It will also host Super Bowl 62 in Feb. 2028. item.title: Game over for Liverpool forward: Talks resume over transfer away
item.description: Game over for Liverpool forward: Talks resume over transfer away Liverpool made big improvements to their frontline over the summer. While the Reds had to contend with the loss of Mohamed Salah they moved decisively for Bradley Barcola and Victor Munoz. With Alexander Isak recovering his form - and Hugo Ekitike in the hunt to return from injury - all of a sudden Andoni Iraola is looking at his options very favourably up top. There is Rio Ngumoha as well as Cody Gakpo to factor in - while Lewis Koumas has proven to be a useful addition to the first-team squad too. What that means is uncertainty over some players already on the books - not least Federico Chiesa . Federico Chiesa is wanted by Inter The Italian, 29, joined Liverpool back in 2024 on a £12.5m deal from Juventus. The Euro 2020 winner secured a contract until 2028 - but so far it’s been a miserable time on Merseyside for Chiesa. Although he can count himself a Premier League title winner things haven’t gone to plan for the former Fiorentina attacker. He has been injured or unavailable for a lot of his time at Anfield thus far - and has rarely pulled up any trees on the occasions he’s featured in the first team . It was speculated over the summer that he would be moving to Inter Milan - so long as the Nerazzurri got rid of Luis Henrique. Alas Cristian Chivu was unable to move on his Brazilian winger - meaning Chiesa stayed. Talks resume for Inter - Chiesa deal A report in Tutto Mercato Web however is now claiming that a January deal to take Chiesa to Inter is ON. Talks have been resumed in recent days between the parties - meaning Chiesa could soon be free to kickstart his career in Serie A. “In recent days, Inter have inquired about long-time favourite Federico Chiesa, who could leave Liverpool in January to return to Serie A and relaunch his career after a difficult period in England,” the report reads. Chiesa is reported to be making around £5m per annum at Liverpool - wage demands beyond the capabilities of most Italian sides. Factor in a transfer fee and very quickly the prospect of a deal disappears for the Italian champions. Nonetheless the report adds that Chivu’s side are plotting a LOAN for Chiesa - a deal which would have a favourable outcome for all parties involved. “A loan deal until June is a viable solution, satisfying the needs of both parties.” What becomes of Chiesa beyond summer remains to be seen - when he will have one year left on his deal.

item.title: Appeal rejected! Arsenal wonderkid Max Dowman slapped with three-match ban after Carabao Cup red card drama
item.description: Fleetwood Town v Arsenal - Carabao Cup Fourth Round - Getty Images Sport Arsenal have suffered a significant setback in their efforts to protect teenage sensation Max Dowman after an independent commission dismissed their appeal against his recent red card. The 16-year-old attacker was sent off during a frustrating Carabao Cup evening for the Gunners, and the club's attempt to overturn the decision has officially fallen flat. Dowman sees red in Carabao Cup exit The 16-year-old was given his marching orders in the 85th minute of Arsenal's Carabao Cup tie against Fleetwood Town. The late dismissal followed a heavy challenge from Harrison Neal, with the teenager reacting poorly and kicking out at his opponent. Mikel Arteta's side ultimately exited the competition on penalties following a tense 1-1 draw. Hoping to spare their academy star a lengthy domestic suspension, the north London club formally challenged the referee's decision on grounds of wrongful dismissal and excessive punishment. FA confirms appeal dismissal Those hopes were quickly dashed when the Football Association shut down Arsenal's attempts to clear the youngster's name. Taking to X on Thursday , an FA spokesperson released a statement confirming that the original on-field decision would be upheld by an independent panel. "An independent Regulatory Commission has dismissed claims of both wrongful dismissal and excessive punishment for Max Dowman," the governing body announced. The statement continued: "The Arsenal player was sent off during their EFL Cup game against Fleetwood Town on Tuesday 27 October and will be suspended for three matches." The FA also clarified that full written reasons for the commission's verdict will be published in due course. Arteta demands emotional control Addressing the media immediately after the midweek defeat, Arteta shed light on his tactical and mental expectations for the squad. While the Spanish manager admitted he had not yet spoken directly to Dowman regarding the dismissal, he hinted at frustration over the lapse in discipline. "When we prepared the context of the match, we were very clear on the things to respect, the things that emotionally we have to dominate, it was very clear," Arteta stated. The incident serves as a harsh learning curve for the highly-rated teenager. First-team opportunities are precious for academy prospects, and a momentary loss of composure has now derailed his immediate integration into the senior setup. Premier League absence looms Dowman is now ruled out of Arsenal’s upcoming domestic schedule, missing pivotal Premier League fixtures against Liverpool, Hull City, and Newcastle. This suspension temporarily deprives Arteta of a promising attacking option as the Gunners navigate a demanding autumn calendar. However, the domestic ban does not carry over to European commitments. item.title: ‘Troy Aikman Is Trying to Get Fired,’ ‘He Wants Out’ — Radio Host Predicts Cowboys Legend Will Force ESPN’s Hand ‘In the Next Few Weeks’
item.description: ‘Troy Aikman Is Trying to Get Fired,’ ‘He Wants Out’ — Radio Host Predicts Cowboys Legend Will Force ESPN’s Hand ‘In the Next Few Weeks’ Troy Aikman’s final season under contract with ESPN has turned into a running conversation about where he goes next. This week brought fresh uncertainty over whether Aikman will remain in broadcasting next season, while he continued to leave the door open to a possible role with the Dallas Cowboys. Moreover, tensions between Aikman and his Monday Night Football partner, Joe Buck, still haven’t fully thawed. Radio host Jason Smith took the speculation a step further on Thursday night, predicting ESPN will make a major call in the weeks ahead. Troy Aikman’s ESPN Limbo Rumbles On Cowboys owner Jerry Jones weighed in Tuesday during his weekly spot on Dallas radio station “105.3 The Fan.” Host Shan Shariff asked whether he would ever give Aikman a major role with the team. Jones answered: “Yes, I could and would… The answer is not necessarily that we’re going to do something more direct with the team at this time, but don’t rule it out. It’s very possible.” Aikman described a conversation with Jones on “KTCK The Ticket,” another Dallas station, saying the owner “was very complimentary if something like that were to ever take place with the idea that we’re not having those conversations at this time.” Jason Smith sees a pattern in all of it: “I feel like Troy Aikman is trying to get fired by ESPN. You’re not making these headlines if you care about broadcasting the rest of the year and the Super Bowl. He wants out.” SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN’s Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer He also added that “ESPN isn’t going to keep putting up with it and they’ll replace him on MNF in the next few weeks.” Those takes, however, were just speculation. Aikman, though, sounded different about the Super Bowl on Cowboys insider Mike Fisher’s YouTube show. That was the weekend before he and Buck called Dallas’ Monday night game against the Philadelphia Eagles: “I’m excited about what the rest of this year holds, and I’m excited to finally get back into the booth for a Super Bowl.” On Wednesday night, Aikman appeared at a Dallas event with veteran journalist Peter King, who was there to discuss his new book, “The Game.” Asked whether he expected to keep calling NFL games in 2027, Aikman said , “I would say there’s a 50-50 chance.” Aikman reportedly signed a five-year, $90 million deal when he and Buck jumped from Fox to ESPN in 2022. That deal runs out in March, a month after Super Bowl LXI is in the books. The Joe Buck Rift Reportedly Behind It All The friction with Buck sits under all of it. Front Office Sports’ Ryan Glasspiegel first reported the rift, an argument between the two before the Oct. 12 Los Angeles Rams-Buffalo Bills game at SoFi Stadium. item.title: Brewers Set To Lose Starting Pitcher to Free Agency
item.description: Dustin May pitches for the Brewers during 2026 World Series. Getty Dustin May celebrates during 2026 World Series. Getty The World Series champion Brewers will have plenty to do this offseason. Just one day after clinching the first title in franchise history, Milwaukee is already dealing with personnel changes. Dustin May is declining his mutual option, electing to enter free agency. The 29-year-old, acquired during the trade deadline, made five appearances this postseason for the Brewers. May should command interest from several teams as a free agent this offseason. Dustin May’s Free Agent Market Getty Dustin May celebrates during 2026 World Series May had a decent first half for the Cardinals, producing a 4.38 ERA and 1.28 WHIP over 21 starts. However, St. Louis’ mediocre record compelled its front office to ship off several contributors at the trade deadline. The contending Brewers pounced, bringing aboard May and reliever JoJo Romero on August 3rd in exchange for two prospects. The right-hander saw his numbers drop across the board in Milwaukee. Over ten starts (36.2 innings), May put up a 5.65 ERA and 1.42 WHIP. Still, manager Pat Murphy turned to the veteran several times in the playoffs. During 11.0 innings this postseason, he allowed seven earned runs (5.73 ERA). After the Brewers clinched their World Series title on Wednesday, May announced that he and his wife are expecting their first child . May, once a highly touted pitcher in the Dodgers ‘ system, has had an up and down MLB career. During his first few years in the majors, he was known as a fireballer. However, numerous injuries prevented May from emerging as an ace. Over the course of six seasons with Los Angeles, he notched a 3.71 ERA and 1.15 WHIP. The Dodgers eventually traded the hurler to the Red Sox on July 31st, 2025. After a brief stint in Boston, May signed a one-year, $12.5 million deal with the Cardinals last offseason. That contract included a $20 million mutual option, where either side could opt out. St. Louis was an ideal landing spot, given the spacious dimensions of Busch Stadium. May, now more of a fly ball pitcher, frequently induces opponents into weak contact. Any team that plays in a pitcher-friendly environment should consider the veteran as a back end option in their rotation. Will Brewers Add to Their Pitching Staff? It’s never too early to start speculating about next season, even for frenzied Brewers fans. If Milwaukee wants to earn a second consecutive title, starting pitching depth could go a long way. Granted, the top end of this rotation is among the best in baseball. NL Cy Young favorite Jacob Misiorowski is the favorite, capable of anchoring any pitching staff. Logan Henderson and Kyle Harrison will provide more front-end depth; both arms possess All-Star upside. Robert Gasser, a breakout star this postseason, will be leaned upon as well. item.title: Hawks’ Quin Snyder reveals ‘growth’ moment that helped break three-game losing streak
item.description: Brett Davis-Imagn Images Hawks’ Quin Snyder reveals ‘growth’ moment that helped break three-game losing streak appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . ATLANTA – After starting the season 2-0, the Atlanta Hawks had lost their last three games coming into their matchup against the Cleveland Cavaliers. They’ve had several problems throughout the course of the week, but nothing was bigger than making shots, which in turn bled into their defense not getting stops when they needed. It looked like that was going to be the case again for the Hawks in the first quarter, where they only scored 16 points. Luckily, they were able to turn things around in the second, and it felt like how things were when they first started the season. They scored 30 points in the second, while only allowing 16 points from the Cavs. “It’s harder to defend when you’re not scoring because they’re running at you,” head coach Quin Snyder said after the game. “But even beyond that, you have to be mentally tough to dig in defensively, and we hung in there with that. Then the offense eventually started; we kind of settled in. That dynamic was a really important one in the game. That’s growth for us.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) It was Aaron Wiggins and Onyeka Okongwu who gave the Hawks the boost they needed in that quarter, and it continued throughout the game. Okongwu has struggled with his 3-point shot to start the season, but he was able to see a few more go down in this one, as he made 4-of-6. “I just kept shooting them,” Okongwu said. “My teammates, coaches and everyone here, they want me to get them up. That’s what I do, and I’m very good at it. Being confident, trusting the process, trusting the work, and knowing that some games, when my 3s aren’t going down, keep shooting them. They’ll go down eventually.” “Sometimes you can get discouraged a little bit by a result, especially if you’re a good shooter and you’re used to seeing the ball go in, and it affects other parts of your game,” Snyder said. “He was knocking down shots, but he didn’t hesitate. It’s been a big push to get him to feel comfortable shooting against closeouts, and when he does that, he also has the ability to put the ball on the floor.” The Hawks didn’t surrender the lead after they got it in the second quarter, and even when the Cavs looked like they were about to make a run, there was either a timely shot or a stop on the defensive end. Kansas City Chiefs offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy shared an encouraging update on his wife, Mia, revealing that her recovery from a shooting incident earlier this year is progressing well. Speaking to reporters Thursday ahead of the Chiefs’ Week 8 matchup against the Denver Broncos, Bieniemy said Mia has been doing well in rehabilitation and recently joined the team’s wives’ trip to Seattle. “She’s doing great,” Bieniemy said, via Matt Derrick of Chiefs Digest. “She actually went on the trip this weekend, she was on the wives trip. She was a rock star, obviously. I was just a has-been. She’s doing great. Her rehab has been going great.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) He also joked about having his wife around during her visit to Kansas City, saying he was probably getting on her nerves. Mia was hospitalized in July after being shot at the family’s Virginia home. Their son, Elijah, was arrested and faces three felony charges. Bieniemy stepped away from the Chiefs during training camp to be with his wife before returning on August 10. Bieniemy has been an integral part of the Chiefs’ success over the years, and the organization gave him the time and space he needed to be with his family. He previously credited Mia for encouraging him to rejoin the team as her recovery progressed. With Mia continuing to recover, Bieniemy can take comfort in her progress while balancing his coaching duties with the Chiefs. Related: The Chiefs beat the brakes off the Broncos in Week 1. item.title: UW Opponent Defensive Preview: Nebraska Cornhuskers
item.description: EUGENE, OR - OCTOBER 17: Oregon Ducks quarterback Dylan Raiola (8) throws on the run against Nebraska Cornhuskers defensive lineman Owen Stoudmire (34) during a college football game between the Oregon Ducks and Nebraska Cornhuskers on October 17, 2026 at Autzen Stadium in Eugene, Oregon. (Photo by Brian Murphy/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images UW and Nebraska face off in Lincoln this weekend for the first time as conference foes. The long and storied history between the two teams stretches exactly 101 years and two weeks to the day between the very first match up in 1925 and this Saturday’s game. That shared history primarily revolves around the four games played during the 1990s when both programs were at their peak. The 1991 game featured a furious second half comeback in Lincoln that built the momentum towards UW’s eventual national championship. The Cornhuskers’ return trip to Seattle in 1992 set the stage for the loudest recorded home crowd in college football history. Five years later, Nebraska returned to Montlake to get their revenge for the previous two games while on their way to their own national championship in 1997 in Tom Osborne’s final season. For these two programs, the current stakes of this weekend’s game are much lower, although not entirely without significance. Both Washington and Nebraska enter Saturday night’s matchup at a crossroads in their seasons. Nebraska sits at 5-2 overall and 2-2 in Big Ten play, but the Cornhuskers are coming off consecutive close losses to Indiana and Oregon. Despite those defeats, Matt Rhule’s team has established itself as one of the league’s most physical and statistically dominant defenses, keeping every game within reach through disciplined play, strong linebacker action, and excellent situational defense. Washington, meanwhile, is 4-3 overall and 1-3 in conference play. The Huskies snapped a three-game losing streak with a 38-26 victory over Purdue before their bye week and arrive in Lincoln needing momentum to salvage their Big Ten campaign. Jedd Fisch’s offense remains heavily dependent on its passing attack, ranking among the conference’s better aerial units, but questions at quarterback and a struggling rushing offense persist. Defensive Overview Over Matt Rhule’s four years at Nebraska, the Cornhuskers have embraced a physical and gritty, defensive-oriented identity as a program. Under first-year defensive coordinator, Rob Aurich, Nebraska has maintained the aggressive, fundamentally sound identity Nebraska built under Rhule. The Cornhuskers rank 14th nationally in scoring defense, 9th in total defense, and are holding opponents to just 171 passing yards and 99 rushing yards per game on average. Their suffocating rushing defense on early downs often position them in 3rd & long passing situations where they pressure packages and blanketing secondary can create plays. item.title: Braves make no-brainer $24M Ronald Acuna Jr., Ozzie Albies decision to keep core intact for 2027
item.description: Braves make no-brainer $24M Ronald Acuna Jr., Ozzie Albies decision to keep core intact for 2027 originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Atlanta Braves have another important offseason ahead of them and need to navigate it correctly, as there are still several areas where the team needs to improve. Not only will they have free agency decisions to make, but they will also need to determine which players to bring back before allowing others to test the market. Atlanta didn't end the season the way it wanted to, losing two consecutive home games to the Los Angeles Dodgers . One of the players who had the toughest time was Ronald Acuña Jr., who was booed by fans. Despite all of that, he made it clear that he wanted to stay in Atlanta. “I want to stay here, that hasn't changed. But I can't control that,” Acuña told the media. The futures of Ozzie Albies and Acuña are in the Braves' hands, as the team recently had to make decisions on both players. Each had a club option for 2027, and Sports Illustrated's Harrison Smajovits believed exercising them should be an easy decision for Atlanta. “It's now officially the offseason, and the Atlanta Braves can get to work, for at least the next month, getting their roster assembled for the 2027 season. Two moves to ensure continuity can be made pretty quickly. They have two club options to exercise this offseason: one for Ozzie Albies and the other for Ronald Acuña Jr. Albies would be due just $7 million. Acuña would get a $17 million check. Both numbers are according to Spotrac. All the Braves have to do is make the obvious decision on both. Yes, these are two very easy calls to make,” Smajovits wrote. The Braves made the easy decision Thursday night, exercising the club options for both Acuña and Albies. “The Braves today exercised options for OF Ronald Acuña Jr. and INF Ozzie Albies for the 2027 season,” the Braves posted. This was a no-brainer for Atlanta, as both decisions were relatively inexpensive and made sense for the organization. Next season, however, could be when the Braves have to decide whether to offer Albies a new contract or move on. The duo consists of two of the Braves' longest-tenured players and two of the few remaining members of the World Series team. At the very least, Atlanta will have both players back for the 2027 season. item.title: Revealed: Why Michael Carrick is 'not surprised' to still be Man Utd manager despite horror run
item.description: Manchester United v AFC Bournemouth - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Michael Carrick has insisted he is "not surprised" to remain in the Manchester United dugout despite the club enduring their most disastrous start to a league season in four decades. The former England international saw his position come under intense scrutiny this week following a dismal 3-0 home defeat at the hands of Bournemouth. Surviving the Old Trafford cull Carrick looked certain to face the axe following Sunday's humiliating loss against the Cherries . That result extended an abysmal winless streak to eight matches in all competition, cementing the club's worst start to a league campaign in 40 years. However, crisis talks were held on Monday between the 45-year-old and the United hierarchy. Despite widespread anticipation of a managerial change, the boardroom ultimately opted to keep him at the helm . This backing comes just months after Carrick penned a new permanent two-year deal in the summer. He had earned the permanent role by securing Champions League football, having originally taken over as a short-term successor to Ruben Amorim in January. Tuning out the noise When pressed on his survival, the former midfielder maintained a defiant stance. He insisted his sole focus remains on rectifying the current crisis on the pitch rather than fearing for his job. "No, I am here to do my job and do my job for the team," Carrick told reporters. "I'm desperate to make us better and improve things, so I'm not surprised, no. I said after the [Bournemouth] game that I didn't expect anything. I was dealing with the performance and the result." Addressing the hostile atmosphere during the Bournemouth defeat, he added: "There was no hiding that the dynamics in the stadium were a bit different from normal. My mind was going through that and digesting that as I mentioned to [the media] after the game. It was purely that my mind was [thinking] 'what do we need to do to improve things?'" No assurances needed Despite the significant delay in the club communicating his continuation, Carrick was adamant that he never sought validation from the boardroom. He acknowledged the immense pressure of the Old Trafford hot seat but dismissed the impact of external speculation. "I don't need any assurances from anyone," he declared. "I totally get the position, get the job, the responsibilities and what comes with that. I don't see it really [outside noise], I see things I need to see. I don't look for it, it doesn't help in any way." Reiterating his commitment to the matchgoing fanbase, Carrick concluded: "I care what the supporters think, what it feels like in the stadium. I genuinely don't take any notice of anything else. I know this job and what it brings." item.title: ‘Needs To Have a Backbone,’ ‘Be a Normal Human’ — Sophie Cunningham Lays Out Demands for Next WNBA Commissioner, Draws Adam Silver Comparison
item.description: 'Needs To Have a Backbone,' 'Be a Normal Human' -- Sophie Cunningham Lays Out Demands for Next WNBA Commissioner, Draws Adam Silver Comparison With Cathy Engelbert set to leave her position as WNBA commissioner at the end of 2026, the search for her successor is an important moment for the league. Sophie Cunningham has a clear idea of what the next leader should bring to the role, and she believes the NBA’s Adam Silver offers a good example. Sophie Cunningham Wants Next WNBA Commissioner to Follow Adam Silver’s Approach to Player Relations Speaking on This Past Weekend w/ Theo Von, Cunningham praised Silver for the relationship he has built with NBA players. She believes the WNBA needs someone similar. “I think Adam Silver does a phenomenal job of having a relationship with his NBA players,” Cunningham said . “And so I just think that’s what we need on the W side.” The Indiana Fever guard then made it clear that the next commissioner must be confident enough to stand by their decisions, explaining: “We need someone to come in here who has a backbone, who’s going to stick to what they do, and hold the standard.” The 30-year-old added that the WNBA needs a common goal that can bring players, owners and other stakeholders together. For her, however, leadership is not just about making major decisions. She also wants the next commissioner to have basic communication skills and show respect to the people working in the league. Cunningham used a hypothetical example of a commissioner walking into a room without even greeting a player to explain her point. “Like, we’re in the room. Like, say hi, be human, be nice,” she said. “I think that’s all we’re really asking for is a little bit of respect and just be a normal human. We’re all trying to work for the same goal. We all want to make the WNBA the best it can be.” SEE ALSO: ‘I’m Proud to Be an American Citizen’ — Sophie Cunningham Makes Her Stance Clear Amid WNBA Finals Anthem Controversy She also stressed that the next leader must maintain open communication and support both players and owners, even when their interests do not always match. Cunningham acknowledged that players will not get everything they ask for, but believes having an open line of communication and mutual respect is essential. These comments build on Cunningham’s earlier thoughts about the commissioner search. She had previously spoken about the importance of player relations and discussed the role with Silver after he reached out to her. Cunningham’s comments come as Engelbert prepares to step down after more than seven years in charge. During her tenure, the WNBA experienced significant growth. In 2024, the league recorded 2.35 million regular-season attendees, a 48% increase from the previous year, while attracting more than 54 million unique viewers across its national television partners. The league has also expanded from 12 teams, with plans to reach 18 by 2030. MORE: ‘She Can’t Believe He Chose Philly,’ ‘2 GOATS’ – Fans React

item.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, October 30, 2026
item.description: The Nigerian Naira opened today, Friday, October 30, 2026, holding firm against the United States Dollar across both the official foreign exchange window and the parallel market, following sustained liquidity interventions by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) and healthy diaspora inflows. At the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM), the spot exchange rate traded at N1,346.86 per dollar during early morning transactions. Commercial banks and corporate importers observed orderly liquidity conditions as FX demand for trade obligations, tuition fees, and capital repatriation continued to be met across authorized channels. In the parallel market, commonly referred to as the black market, street traders and Bureau De Change operators across major economic centers, including Lagos, Abuja, and Kano, quoted buying rates around N1,375 per dollar, while selling rates hovered around N1,385 per dollar. The price gap between the official market and the parallel window remains narrow. Financial analysts attribute the relative stability of the local currency to Nigeria’s solid foreign reserve buffer, which remains well above $55 billion, enabling the central bank to cushion short-term demand shocks and maintain stability across trading channels. Market experts expect trading to remain steady throughout the business day as routine demand is steadily absorbed by market liquidity.
